summary: Formats the next lap time into an output buffer for HUD/replay display. Computes the next lap index (current lap counter at dword_7C54E0+16448 incremented by 1, wrapped 2->0), copies the empty prefix string asc_5CCE18 into the buffer, then selects the time source: when byte_7CFFF0 bit 0 is set it resolves the ghost car index via sub_4D1B50(0) (returning 0 without formatting when the index is 255/invalid) and reads flt_5F0780[4656*index+lap]; otherwise it reads the float at dword_7C54E0+4*lap+16552. The float is written into the first 4 bytes of the output buffer, and when it is positive the value is split via SpatialGridCell and appended with StringFormatWithBufferOverflowCheck as " %.2d:%06.3f".

operations.description: v2 = (lap counter at dword_7C54E0+16448) + 1, wrapped to 0 when the counter equals 2; selects the next lap index.
strcpy copies the empty prefix string asc_5CCE18 into the output buffer a1; v3 retains the buffer pointer for the later append.
When byte_7CFFF0 bit 0 is set, use the ghost/replay timing source; otherwise read the race-struct lap time.
Resolve the ghost/replay car index via sub_4D1B50(0).
If the ghost index is 255 (invalid), return 0 without formatting anything.
v5 = flt_5F0780[4656 * ghostIndex + nextLapIndex]; the ghost lap time selected by car index and lap index.
v5 = *(float*)(dword_7C54E0 + 4*nextLapIndex + 16552); the race-struct lap time for the next lap.
Write v5 as a float into the first 4 bytes of the output buffer a1.
Formatting is only attempted when v5 > 0.0 (a valid lap time).
SpatialGridCell splits the float seconds value into minute/second components used for display.
Append the formatted string via StringFormatWithBufferOverflowCheck(v3, " %.2d:%06.3f", minutes, seconds) into the buffer.

unresolved: flt_59E440, a2d063f_1 and dword_8ACEE0 are listed as packet globals but do not appear in the raw source; their role is unknown.
Meaning of the hardcoded offsets 16448 / 16552 and the 4656 stride are inferred (lap counter / lap-time array); not independently confirmed.
Literal character '\' (backslash) is used as the strcpy prefix; the exact content of asc_5CCE18 was not verified.
